prompt: Prime-time adult animated sitcom characters with simple rounded cartoon bodies, flat colour and black outlines, but every face is painted with startling real skin: pores, stubble, wrinkles, wet tired eyes, real eyelids, far more lifelike than anything around it, no feature exaggerated. Every colour is laid on in thick visible oil brushstrokes. Night, the camera low at table height among the food in a smoky 1930s back room: the glazed edge of a carved ham and a tall champagne glass fill the near foreground on the left. Large in frame just beyond them, off-centre right, a tall skinny mayor in a bowler hat with a gold chain and a napkin tucked in his collar: a long narrow face, hollow cheeks, a pencil-thin grey moustache, frozen mid-chew with his cheek full and his fork raised, only his eyes swivelled sideways towards the door. Behind him, small and soft in the far wall, an open doorway of cold blue light with a heavy-set Black baker standing in it in a vest, one small loaf in his hand, a dark shape. Two gangsters in pinstripes at the table edge, frozen the same way, forks in the air. One low brass lamp with a green glass shade hangs just above, pooling amber across the mayor's face and the grease on his chin; cigar smoke in flat layers under the lamp, a candle stub in a bottle. Most of the frame in deep brown shadow; the brightest values are the lamp's pool on his face and the food, and the blue doorway. Plain margins with no writing. Thanks.
